game.name: ASHVALE Atlas
game.description: New in Atlas 1.7: the sun and the moon at their true scale, as ours are to the Earth - the moon a quarter of the planet across, sixty planet radii out, on game time, turning copper when it passes through the planet's shadow, and when it crosses the sun its shadow falls on the planet and you can watch it travel. North and south have changed places: Ashvale lies in the northern hemisphere. In 1.6: the seasons. The planet's axis leans, so through the 365-day game year the sun climbs north and sinks south of the equator: the poles get their long summer days and their long winter nights, and the line between day and night tilts with the season - the same sun that lights the game. In 1.5: the sun now circles the planet every two hours, as day and night do in the game. In 1.4: the moon. It follows the real one - you can see it in space, lit by the sun so it shows its phase - and the night side of the planet is as bright as the moon is full. In 1.3 the sun. It circles the planet once a day, lighting one side while the other lies in night, and you can see it out in space. And your contacts. Players who have you in their address book, and you them, show as orange dots with their name while they play (the arcade asks you first; contact links are kept in memory only, never stored). In 1.2 a compass rose that turns with you (tap it to face north), the equator drawn round the planet and both poles marked, saguaro cactus in the deserts, and woods with a way through everywhere. In 1.1 you are here. Signed in, the Atlas shows a blue dot where your ASHVALE character last stood, and the You button flies you down to it. The whole ASHVALE planet in one view: start from orbit and zoom all the way down to the ground, seamlessly. Two continents in a wide ocean, island chains, rivers from mountain creeks to the sea, deserts, rainforest, taiga and snowy ranges, Ashvale village and the harbour town of Saltmere. Drag to pan, scroll or pinch to zoom, right-drag to turn.
